subject: Briefing: answers on prompt PII lifecycle and next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Aug 2029 13:15:00 +0000
Subject: Briefing: answers on prompt PII lifecycle and next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier. Per our call, summarized below are the concrete answers on how Redwood treats prompts and derivatives (PII, retention, logging, residency) and the suggested next steps so your security and engineering teams can evaluate. This is intentionally concise — let me know if you want formal language for legal.

What we store by default (hosted API):
- Request/response telemetry (non-tokenized traces): retained for 30 days for SLO/ops and debugging.
- Full token-level request/response logs are not persisted by default; they can be enabled for a bounded window if needed for debugging.
- Prompt derivatives (embeddings or extracted vectors): NOT stored unless you opt-in. If opt-in, stored in the region you select and retained per contract (default opt-in TTL = 90 days).
- KV caches live in-memory on inference pods and are ephemeral — they are not written to disk unless you enable a persistent cache (rare).

Controls available to you:
- Ephemeral-only mode: turn on zero-retention (TTL=0) for hosted traffic; no long-term logs or derivatives are kept.
- Regional residency: for hosted, we can pin storage to a specific region (US / EU / APAC). For enterprise Private deployments, everything stays inside your VPC.
- Encryption & keys: customer-managed KMS supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted uses envelope encryption with HSM-backed keys.
- Audit logs: admin-level audit trails (who accessed what) are available and can be retained per your SaaS plan.

Our baseline compliance artifacts: SOC 2 Type II snapshot attached (SOC2-snapshot-2029.pdf).

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm whether you need embeddings stored or prefer ephemeral-only for the pilot.
2) If embeddings are required, confirm retention target (we recommend 90 days for model performance; can be lowered).
3) Legal: we can accept DPA redlines; I attached a version with suggested callouts (DPA-redlines.docx) and a DocuSign link if you want to sign.
4) Technical deep-dive with Dev and your infra/security team next week to validate KMS and region settings.

If that summary looks right I can lock into a short SOW for a 6-week pilot with the options you choose.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
https://www.redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot-2029.pdf (pdf), DPA-redlines.docx (docx)

From: Samir Patel <samir@heliumhealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Chen <lauren.chen@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Aug 2029 10:12:14 +0300
Subject: Re: Briefing: answers on prompt PII lifecycle and next steps

Thanks Aisha — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions from our security and product teams:  

1) If a clinician submits PHI in the prompt (name, MRN, notes), will that appear anywhere in persisted logs by default? You said token logs are not persisted by default, but want to confirm what "request/response telemetry" contains.

2) If we opt into embedding storage for search/recall, are embeddings reversible in any way to reveal PHI?

3) For caching: if we enable a persistent cache (you mentioned rare cases), is the cache encrypted-at-rest and can it be pinned to our APAC region?

4) Retention: our legal wants retention <= 90 days for any stored derivatives, and ideally 30 days for requests. Are those defaults configurable per-contract?

5) Can you confirm whether debugging logs include full prompt text or only hashed identifiers?

We want to move quickly but need these answers to present to our CISO. Can you loop in the engineering contact who can confirm the technical guarantees?

—Samir
Head of Product, Helium Health

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Aug 2029 11:05:30 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Briefing: answers on prompt PII lifecycle and next steps (technical clarifications)

Aisha / Ben — quick technical clarifications I asked to prepare for Samir's questions so we can respond with precise guarantees. Paste below for record.

- Request/response telemetry: contains request/response metadata (latency, model, token counts, error traces) and a short non-tokenized summary used for alerting. We do NOT persist token-level text by default.

- Full token logs: when enabled for debugging, they are written to an encrypted blob store for a bounded window (default 30 days) and accessible only to ops via RBAC; we mark access in audit logs. This is opt-in and requires approval.

- Embeddings: vectors are non-reversible in practice (no known algorithm to reconstruct plaintext reliably). We additionally support deterministic hashing of identifiers prior to vectorization if customer requests. When stored, embeddings are encrypted at rest and can be stored in the customer-selected region. Default opt-in TTL = 90 days; can be contractually reduced to any value >= 0.

- KV cache: standard mode is in-memory LRU on inference pods (ephemeral). Persistent cache option stores encrypted blobs in a region-bound store and is only used for stateful workloads; it is configurable per-deployment and encrypted-at-rest with customer KMS for Dedicated/Private.

- Debugging logs & redaction: we can configure automatic prompt redaction (masking PII patterns) before any persistence.

I recommend offering Samir a written configuration matrix: (1) Ephemeral-only (no persistent logs, no embeddings stored), (2) Hosted with opt-in embeddings + 90d TTL, (3) Dedicated/Private with KMS + custom TTLs.

– Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Chen <lauren.chen@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2029 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Briefing: answers on prompt PII lifecycle and next steps

Samir — thanks for the questions, and good call bringing Lauren. Short answers and proposed configuration for your CISO review:  

1) PHI in prompts: by default, PHI will NOT be persisted at token level. Our default "request/response telemetry" captures metadata and non-tokenized summaries only. If you enable token-level debugging, that is stored only for a bounded window (we suggest 30d) and access is controlled via RBAC + audit logs.

2) Embeddings reversibility: embeddings are not considered reversible; we also offer deterministic hashing of identifiers upstream of vectorization. If you opt-in to embeddings for search, we will store them encrypted and in the APAC region per your request. We can set the TTL to 90 days or lower (you requested <=90 days).

3) Persistent cache: only enabled if you ask — we will not enable it for the pilot. If you require it later, it will be encrypted-at-rest and can be region-pinned; for Dedicated/Private you can use your own KMS.

4) Retention controls: yes — both telemetry and derivatives TTLs are contract-configurable. Hosted defaults: telemetry = 30d, embeddings opt-in TTL = 90d. We can set both to 30d for the pilot if that helps your approval.

5) Debugging logs: redaction options available. We can provide a config that strips or hashes PII before any persistence.

Next steps we propose:  
- Option A (recommended pilot): Hosted with ephemeral token logs, embeddings OFF. If you need embeddings for search, we can run a short architecture that keeps embeddings for 30d and stores them in APAC.
- Option B: Dedicated trial with KMS and explicit 30d TTL across telemetry and embeddings.

I've attached SOC2 snapshot and our suggested DPA redlines. If that aligns, Ben will put together a short SOW and I can schedule the technical follow-up with Dev for Thursday.
